column3: It directly states that every creature's provision rests with Allah, while adding His knowledge of each creature's settled and temporary place.
It adds that expansion and restriction of provision are both Allah's measured governance rather than a creature's self-supply.
Safe conduct for an uninformed seeker gives a limited practical setting for Allah's hearing and knowledge, not provision itself.
Allah's ownership of all that rests by night and day broadens the focus's creaturely scope around His hearing and knowledge.
The preceding certainty of death places worldly provision within a temporary life, without explaining its source.
Seeking refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Knowing gives a practical response to threat that complements reliance on the Provider.
Its assurance of return to Allah shares the focus's closing attributes but adds no account of provision.
The immediately preceding praise of those who rely on their Lord supplies the response to the focus's provision assurance.
The identical divine attributes confirm the focus's ending but contribute no further context.
Allah's knowledge of speech in heaven and earth slightly particularizes the focus's hearing and knowledge.
It directly continues the theme by describing Allah's widening and restricting provision for His servants.
Human transport over land and sea and provision of good things present mobility itself as sustained divine provision.
It directly counters fear of poverty by affirming provision for both children and parents.
It adds that what is spent is replaced, making provision a continuing divine supply rather than a fixed possession.
Livestock that carry loads are included among what Allah provides, giving a concrete animal-related extension.
The town's abundance, then hunger and fear after ingratitude, shows provision as a divine favor with moral consequence.
The nearby promise of an enduring dwelling rewards faithful action but does not develop earthly provision.
Every creature's prostration establishes creaturely dependence on Allah without addressing provision.
The repeated divine attributes support the focus's conclusion but add only the firmness of Allah's word.
Its appeal to Allah as creator of the heavens and earth supplies a nearby grounding for assigning provision to Him.
The inclusion of creatures in universal prostration reinforces their dependence, not their provision.
It displays the dispersion and gathering of creatures as signs of divine power, only indirectly related to their sustenance.
Its contrast between worldly diversion and the living final abode gives a limited horizon for reliance on present provision.
The carrying of Noah's descendants offers a distant transport image but no provision link.
Allah's sufficiency amid religious opposition gives a general reliance theme, while the shared attributes are otherwise redundant.
Provision for those killed in Allah's way extends divine sustaining beyond visible earthly life.
Its statement about examples and learned comprehension does not clarify creatures, provision, or the divine attributes in focus.
The destruction of unjust towns does not add to the focus's account of provision.
Rain reviving dead land supplies a nearby sign of Allah's life-giving power that supports the provision claim.
Spending from what Allah has provided shows recipients as conduits of provision rather than its final holders.
Allah's knowledge of hidden emergence offers a bounded parallel to His knowing creatures' unspoken needs.
It restates the divine widening and restricting of provision, though the principle is already established above.
It links belief and spending to what Allah has provided, adding an ethical use of received provision.
Allah's knowledge of every pregnancy's hidden bearing sharpens the focus's claim that He knows needs beyond human speech.
Calling on Allah alone for rescue at sea gives the local setting a reliance-under-peril dimension.
Its barred hearing of the highest assembly is unrelated to creaturely provision or divine care.
The fate of towns that expelled the Messenger gives a concrete displacement setting adjacent to reliance beyond one's home.
It describes provision as divinely widened or restricted with full awareness of servants, despite its redundancy.
Its warning of punishment for wrongdoers does not develop the focus.
Passing heedlessly by signs in heaven and earth does not clarify provision or its recipients.
The local warning against enjoying what was given ungratefully only indirectly frames provision as a gift.
Divine testimony to revelation does not add to the focus's provision or creaturely scope.
Allah's knowledge of pregnancy and birth echoes hidden creaturely conditions but is weaker than the earlier parallel.
Playing in idle discourse has no material link to the focus.
Provision of good things to a vulnerable, threatened community gives a social example of support after insecurity.
The punishment of disobedient towns does not explain the focus's provision claim.
The local contrast of sanctuary safety and divine favor extends the surrounding argument about security and gratitude.
Bearing a lasting burden in the hereafter does not illuminate animals not carrying provision.
Allah's ownership of heaven and earth supports His authority to provide, but adds no specific sustenance dimension.
Rain restoring the earth provides an indirect natural sign of Allah's life-giving care.
Allah's knowledge of concealed and open speech modestly develops the focus's closing attribute.
Perseverance in battle does not clarify provision or creaturely dependence.
The local condemnation of fabricated falsehood does not add to the focus.
Allah's favor and knowledge give a broad dependence theme without a provision connection.
The plea not to be burdened beyond capacity only loosely contrasts with the focus's image of creatures not carrying provision.
It repeats measured widening and restricting of provision, now explicitly noting that many people do not understand it.
Its judgment about desert dwellers and revealed limits does not illuminate the focus.
The mention of creatures in deferred punishment is not about their provision.
The local promise of guidance for striving supports reliance on Allah but not the focus's particular provision image.
Noah's carrying of paired creatures offers a distinct preservation and transport image alongside the focus's unburdened creatures.
The eschatological creature from the earth does not develop provision or reliance.
Its direct question and answer that Allah provides from heaven and earth reinforces exclusive divine provision.
The sleepers entrust uncertain knowledge to their Lord while arranging careful food and safety, adding a practical reliance setting.
The animal simile concerns desire and rejection, not creaturely provision.
Mutual non-liability for deeds does not bear on the focus.
Divine clarification before judgment does not explain provision or the focus's attributes.
Expulsion for faith gives a limited migration context, but no link to the provision assurance.
Its reflection on Qarun's fall reaffirms that Allah widens and restricts provision, now against wealth-based illusion.
Carrying a load is too isolated to clarify creatures not carrying their provision.
The appointed provision of the blessed gives only a brief afterlife parallel.
Wealth and children are shown as a false ground of security, indirectly qualifying assumptions about provision.
The limits of those who seek only near life do not clarify the focus's provision claim.
Trusting the All-Hearing, All-Knowing amid an uncertain peace offer provides a concrete model of reliance under incomplete knowledge.
Provision descending from the sky and reviving the earth gives a natural sign of the Provider's sustaining activity.
Its good provision for believers gives a distinct final-reward extension but not the focus's creaturely dependence.
The inability of false objects of worship to cause harm or benefit indirectly supports turning to Allah as sole provider.
It joins creation, renewal, and provision in an argument for Allah's exclusive agency.
The terse future knowledge warning has no specific relation to the focus.
Encouragement not to weaken in conflict does not clarify divine provision.
Rain reviving land is not presented here as provision and adds little after the closer natural signs.
Calling disbelievers the worst creatures does not develop the provision of creatures.
The repeated divine attributes occur in a different personal trial and add no further focus-specific insight.
Its contrast between usury and charity does not explain the focus's provision assurance.
Enjoyment and deferred knowledge are not a meaningful provision link here.
Mercy from the All-Hearing, All-Knowing gives a broad care theme, though it remains nonspecific.
Provision from the sky is explicitly a sign, connecting material supply to recognition of its Giver.
The earth and mountains being carried at the end does not clarify the focus's living creatures.
Allah's complete hearing and knowledge console against hostile speech, a remote reliance parallel.
Recompense for truthfulness and hypocrisy does not add to the focus.
Personal awareness of what was brought forward does not illuminate provision or divine sustenance.
The law of accidental killing is unrelated to the focus.
Its denial of knowledge behind a false claim does not develop the focus's divine knowledge or provision.
Allah's witnessing of every affair gives a general omniscience parallel but no creaturely provision insight.
Its rejection and future knowledge warning do not bear on the focus.
Rules for eating in households provide a distant social-food connection without explaining provision.
Leaving opponents with a peace word does not clarify the focus.
Creation and proportioning from a drop do not add to creaturely provision.
Lack of knowledge about the highest assembly does not bear on the focus.
Divine knowledge of inner thoughts in battle does not add to the focus's sustaining claim.
The sealing of hearing and perception warns that knowledge may not yield receptivity, a remote boundary for the focus's attributes.
It commands seeking provision from Allah alone, directly joining the focus's claim about provision to the worship and reliance it calls for.
It names Allah as the Provider, giving the focus's attribution of creatures' and human provision its most explicit formulation.
It promises a way out and provision from an unanticipated source for the God-conscious, directly extending reliance beyond visible means.
It pairs provision from where one does not expect with trust in Allah, closely explaining the focus's call to depend on the Provider.
Its challenge of who can provide if Allah withholds provision directly reinforces that no other source can replace Him.
It gathers creation, provision, death, and restoration under Allah's agency, placing the focus's provision claim within a full life-cycle argument.
It asks whether any creator besides Allah provides from heaven and earth, directly asserting His exclusive sustaining agency.
Its question of who provides from heaven and earth makes the focus's answer part of a direct argument for recognizing Allah.
It forbids killing children from poverty while affirming Allah provides for parents and children, closely paralleling provision despite material fear.
It locates promised provision beyond immediate human control, adding an unseen horizon to the focus's creaturely reliance.
The command to eat Allah's lawful, good provision and thank Him gives the human response to the provision affirmed in the focus.
Eating from what Allah has provided while avoiding excess adds a responsibility accompanying received provision.
The command to eat from the Lord's provision and give thanks presents provision as a communal gift requiring gratitude.
It exposes the refusal to spend from what Allah has provided, reinforcing that provision received from Him should circulate to others.
It declares the Lord's provision better, distinguishing divine provision from any hoped-for human recompense.
The distribution of livelihood among people explains provision as an ordered divine apportionment rather than self-made status.
Allah's differing measures of provision challenges the assumption that possession makes its holder an independent source.
It records the human tendency to read generous provision as personal honor, qualifying how abundance should be understood.
It records the corresponding mistake of reading restricted provision as humiliation, clarifying the focus's wider theme of measured provision.
The confession that Allah has provided good provision grounds faithful action in received divine support.
Provision of fruits in a secure sanctuary links divine sustenance with protection against fears of displacement.
Rain, fruits, ships, and rivers display several channels through which Allah sustains human life.
Families and good things are presented as Allah's provision, broadening the focus beyond food to human life and continuity.
The command to eat from sacrificial animals and feed others shows provision shared across need rather than privately carried.
The command to eat and drink from Allah's provision gives a direct human counterpart to creatures receiving their sustenance.
Believers are commanded to eat the good things Allah has provided and to give thanks, joining provision to worship.
It directs believers to consume the lawful good provision of Allah with reverence, adding an ethical boundary to receiving it.
The question about forbidding Allah's adornment and good provision challenges human attempts to control what Allah has supplied.
Seeking Allah's bounty after prayer gives an active human posture that remains oriented to the divine source of provision.
Walking the earth and eating from Allah's provision illustrates creaturely movement without treating mobility as self-sustenance.
Its declaration that Allah's earth is spacious gives a migration-and-reliance setting that helps frame the immediate context of the focus.
